findings.title: Required legacy owner trajectory cannot commit
findings.detail: The genuine legacy preparation owners reach COMMIT_READY with S37.ref_s34_id pointing to Nutrition and S35.ref_s34_id pointing to Fitness. prepare_authorization_basis requires those IDs to be equal unless full_execution_members is present, and denies the actual legacy CommitBundle with 'policy, demand, and calendar authorization bounds must exist'. The named source_owner_trajectories_dc execution has 1 failed/1 passed; source_suite_dc has 1 failed/105 passed. Legacy T6 and subsequent START/PAUSE/RESUME/CONTINUE therefore do not satisfy the packet's positive oracle. This is a pre-existing producer/consumer compatibility issue, honestly recorded as BLOCKED/FAIL, but it prevents this packet from passing. The packet restricts transactions.py changes to full source validation/freshness, so closing this requires authorized scope/packet resolution and fresh tests/review; replacing the positive test with an expected denial cannot close it. The later synthetic certificate mismatch is static evidence only and was not reached.

findings.title: Mandatory unchanged hosted DB regression is not evidenced
findings.detail: The packet additionally requires the existing legacy/full preparation, execution, demo, factset, preparation, interleaving and transaction-interface suites to execute positively through unchanged hosted full PostgreSQL CI. The reviewed revision's execution ledger contains only the own source DB suite and normal non-DB commands; it contains no hosted full DB CI execution/result. Fixture corrections in the older suites are therefore not independently established as positive regression evidence at this revision. Obtain successful SHA-bound unchanged hosted DB CI before any PASS or merge recommendation; local foreign lifecycles are not an allowed substitute. This is an outstanding evidence gate, not an observed failure in those unexecuted older suites.
